text:
Viktor Arvidsson is 33, on his fifth NHL team after a season in Boston, and in his first year in Detroit he's still doing the thing he's always done: going to the front of the net. He has 10.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances), more than his 8 actual goals.

The stretch since his hat trick against Chicago on Oct. 29 has been grim. He has no goals in nine games on 2.9 expected, and our numbers call that one due. He's also pointless in seven straight, and there the chances have thinned, which is less reassuring. Detroit has scored 3.65 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, and the Red Wings have been losing.

His game hasn't changed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for scoring chances from the slot last season, carrying the puck in on 58% of his entries. When a player keeps getting there, the goals usually follow. On a team that badly needs some, he's one of the likelier sources.
headline: Arvidsson still finds the net front, but not the net
